A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AutoSteer work. The complete main texts, equations, table, figures and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched across the versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original AutoSteer safety and utility results in Table 1, layer and steering-intensity analyses, and qualitative cases in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments on LLaVA-OV and Chameleon, including quantitative results, diagnostic analyses and appendix case studies.

M1.justification: SAS-based layer selection, the 64-unit MLP safety prober, threshold gating and LM-Steer-based refusal head remain unchanged. Revised explanations do not establish a different algorithm or training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain VLSafe and ToViLaG-based training and evaluation, the three toxicity configurations, and RealWorldQA/MMMU utility evaluation. Appendix F retains the same three scenario categories and nine cases.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the original-model and Steer (LM-Steer) comparators for both evaluated models. Newly cited HiddenDetect is discussed as related work but is not added to the experimental comparison.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendices A, B and G retain the sample sizes, data construction, model configurations, selected layers, threshold 0.5, evaluation intensity 0.1 and judging procedures. No revised evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Appendix D revises the qualitative demonstration of excessive-steering corruption, adding an explicit input query and changing the displayed response excerpts. The intensity sweep, SAS analyses, toxicity-score counterexamples and Appendix F cases remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Table 1 retains differences from the original model in parentheses, including ±0.0; these are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Appendix D changes the reported corrupted-output example, replacing the earlier excerpts with a revised banana-query response. Table 1 values and all plotted results remain identical, including AutoSteer VLSafe ASRs of 4.2% and 15.4% for LLaVA-OV and Chameleon.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 revises the displayed BLIP-2 composition from Text to E_txt(Text), explicitly incorporating text encoding into the formal expression. AutoSteer's mathematical definitions and equations otherwise remain unchanged; equation renumbering adds no theory.

C1.justification: The conclusion replaces the explicit claim of exceptional effectiveness where traditional steering falls short with a general statement of effectiveness in multimodal safety scenarios. The abstract, principal contributions and safety–utility claims remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix E.1 make the representation-based explanation of Chameleon's image-only failures more tentative, changing likely explanations to possible ones. The substantive limitations concerning training data, internal representations, calibration and model coverage are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link on the first page and supplies the input query for Appendix D's corruption example. Existing implementation settings, evaluation prompts and Appendix G reproducibility information were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds Song et al. (2025)'s multimodal-model survey and Jiang et al. (2025)'s HiddenDetect, including a short description of hidden-state-based jailbreak detection. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized prose edits refine the background, method explanations, results discussion and conclusion. v2 also updates affiliation/contact information, adds acknowledgments and expands future-work plans. The main section sequence and Appendix A–G organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 boxes and italicizes construction and evaluation prompts in Appendices A–B, numbers previously unnumbered background equations and relocates Figure 8 within Appendix D. Table 1 and all 25 figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves accessibility and documentation through code-access information, clearer prompt formatting and an explicit input for the corruption example. Added related work and a more restrained comparative conclusion also help. The experiments and numerical evidence are unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
